title: Multiples & Common Multiples

els.text: List in order. Find a match. Circle it.

A multiple of a number is the result of multiplying it by a whole number. 

It is a multiple if it is in the numbers times tables e.g. 20 is in the 5 times tables, so 20 is a multiple of 5.
Write the first five multiples of 15.

slides.brief: 0–3 minutes, after the definition. Reveal each new multiple with an arrow from the previous term and +15 underneath the arrow; a times-table grid is optional support.
slides.title: Listing multiples

els.text: Start with the number. Keep adding that number.

slides.title: Multiples book work

els.text: A common multiple is a number that is a multiple of both numbers.
Write both lists. Which number is in both?
54 is a common multiple: it is in both lists.

slides.brief: 21–25 minutes. First stop and circle 54 in both lists. Then ask whether another shared number exists; extend to 108 and circle it. Do not name LCM until the next slide.
slides.title: Find a common multiple

els.text: The lowest common multiple (LCM) is the smallest positive multiple shared by both numbers.
No match yet? Keep listing in order.
LCM = 48. It is the smallest number in both lists.

slides.brief: 26–29 minutes. Initially show two entries per list, with no match. Extend the lists to 48; circle both 48s. Equal list lengths are not a stopping rule.
slides.title: Find the lowest common multiple
